The cardiac cycle has three phases: contraction (systole), which ejects blood; relaxation (diastole), during which the chambers fill; and a brief period of complete rest before the cycle repeats. My earlier two-phase answer folded that resting period into diastole, so this three-part breakdown is the more standard one. The question appears to be cut off, so this assumes the usual textbook sequence.
